key_insight: High-dimensional function approximation has a lattice-ball regime with cost scaling as d^(R²)/(R²!), polynomial in dimension d for fixed R, rather than the familiar hypercube cost R^d.
engineering_relevance: When R² ≪ d, this regime can substantially reduce spectral approximation costs without requiring special function spaces or error norms.
method: Approximate analytic or m-times continuously differentiable functions using orthogonal spectral series.
Study Fourier, Chebyshev, and Legendre expansions through lattice-point counting inside hyperspheres.
Identify the discrete lattice-ball scaling regime when R² ≪ d.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical illustrations on MNIST digit classification and solution-operator learning for Burgers’ and radiative transfer equations, but gives no quantitative performance metrics.
watch_item: Polynomial scaling assumes fixed R; if the approximation scale required for accuracy grows with dimension, the cost advantage must be reassessed.
paper_title: Second scaling regime in high-dimensional function approximation and curse of dimensionality
